title: On-demand precision unwrapping for streaming prefill/decode to reduce dequant overhead
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: In streaming workloads (short prefills + many decode steps) we observe tail latency spikes when switching between quantized (INT8/FP8) attention kernels and host-side FP16/FP32 code paths due to repeated dequantization + memory copies.

Goal: Implement an on-demand precision unwrapping mechanism that avoids eager global dequant for batched streaming requests. The feature should: 1) keep activation tensors in packed/quantized layout as long as possible, 2) provide fast local kernel-level unwrapping hooks when a decode path requires higher precision, and 3) integrate with the kernel selection scorer so routing decisions penalize expensive dequant transitions.

Accepted behavior: 1) end-to-end 95th percentile latency for streaming generation workloads with batch sizes 1-8 improves by >=15% compared to current master for INT8/FP8-enabled models; 2) memory overhead increase <10%; 3) no regressions on non-quantized workloads; 4) feature toggle controlled at model-config level; 5) observable KPIs emitted (dequant_count, dequant_latency_ms, precision_path_chosen).

Proposed approach:
- Add a small per-request 'precision-intent' tag propagated through prefill -> KV cache -> decode. Kernels that support in-place or fused unwrapping expose a lightweight callback to convert on first use instead of a global prefill step.
- Extend kernel selection scorer to include a transition cost estimate (based on recent dequant_count histogram and measured dequant_latency_ms) when computing the best precision path.
- Implement a lazy dequant adapter for attention prefills: for batched prefill we keep the KV cache in compact quant layout and only unwrap slices touched by cross-attention or by incompatible ops.
- Provide two-mode rollout: conservative (only unwrap for incompatible ops) and aggressive (allow on-demand unwrap to maximize quant path usage).

Experiment plan:
1) Microbench: measure per-kernel unwrap cost for INT8->FP16 and FP8->FP16 on A100 and H100. Record dequant_latency_ms distribution.
2) Integration: implement lazy-unwrapping prototype behind runtime flag and run end-to-end streamer benchmarks (LLama-2-13B and Llama-2-70B variants) with synthetic and real prompt traces.
3) Safety checks: run precision-regression eval suite and end-to-end deterministic tests.

Rollout:
- Feature behind model_config flag and runtime feature flag.
- Canary on internal dedicated cluster with traffic shadowing (2% traffic) -> ramp 10% -> 50% -> 100% conditioned on no SLO regressions and dequant metrics within thresholds.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- New metrics: runtime.dequant_count, runtime.dequant_latency_ms_p50/p95, runtime.precision_transitions, runtime.precision_path_choice.
- Dashboard: per-model breakdown and per-route latency correlation with precision transitions.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Aggressive lazy unwrapping may increase memory fragmentation and complicate KV eviction policies.
- Some fused kernels (custom matmuls) cannot operate on partially unwrapped buffers; need fallback path detection and safe compat checks.
- Whether to store precision intent in the serialized KV cache for Private deployments (compatibility and storage cost).
